title: Milk Coming Out of a Baby's Nose: What Parents Should Know

blocks.narration: Seeing milk come out of your baby's nose after a feed can be scary, but it is not always an emergency.
captions: Milk from the nose can look scary
but it is not always an emergency
visual_keywords: calm parent holding baby at home

blocks.narration: In young babies, spit up is common because the feeding and reflux system is still maturing. Sometimes milk comes back up and exits through the nose.
captions: Spit up is common in young babies
Milk can sometimes come through the nose

blocks.narration: Feeding in a slightly upright position, slowing a fast feed, and taking small pauses may help reduce spit up.
visual_keywords: parent holding baby upright after feeding

blocks.narration: After feeding, hold your baby upright for a little while. For sleep, keep your baby flat on the back on a safe sleep surface.
captions: For sleep: flat on the back
visual_keywords: parent holding baby upright after feeding
baby sleeping on back in crib

blocks.narration: Call a doctor urgently if vomiting is forceful, green, yellow, or bloody, or if your baby has trouble breathing, refuses feeds, has fewer wet diapers, or is not gaining weight.
If milk comes through the nose often, or feeding is hard, your pediatrician can check for other causes, including anatomy of the palate. Do not try to diagnose it at home.
